_note: Original advanced concept questions for queues.

questions.title: FIFO order
questions.code:
Queue state, front -> back:
A, B, C

Operation:
dequeue()
questions.prompt: A queue receives A, then B, then C. One item is removed. Which item comes out?
questions.explanation: A queue is first-in, first-out. A was added first, so A leaves first.

questions.title: Queue front
questions.code:
Queue state, front -> back:
red, blue, green

Operation:
peek()
questions.prompt: What does `peek` or `front` return in a queue?
choices: The oldest item without removing it
The newest item and removes it
questions.explanation: Peek/front reads the next item that would be dequeued, but leaves it in the queue.

questions.title: Dequeue trace
questions.explanation: The dequeue removes 2. The oldest remaining value is 5.

questions.title: Wrong removal end
questions.code:
Queue attempt:
add A to back
add B to back
remove from back
questions.prompt: A queue implementation adds to the back but also removes from the back. What behavior did it create?
questions.explanation: Adding and removing from the same end removes the newest item first, which is stack behavior.

questions.title: BFS structure
questions.code:
BFS waiting line:
front [start-neighbor-1, start-neighbor-2] back

Next node comes from the front.
questions.prompt: Which structure helps breadth-first search process nodes level by level?
questions.explanation: A queue processes older discovered nodes first, which keeps BFS level by level.

questions.title: Deque meaning
questions.code:
Deque idea:
front <-> [A, B, C] <-> back

Both ends can add or remove.
choices: A double-ended queue that can add or remove at both ends
A queue that can only remove from the back
questions.explanation: A deque opens both ends, so it can support stack-like or queue-like operations.

questions.title: Priority queue
questions.prompt: How is a priority queue different from a regular FIFO queue?
choices: The oldest item always leaves first
questions.explanation: A priority queue removes by priority, not plain arrival order.

questions.title: BFS queue steps
questions.prompt: Arrange the main queue steps for BFS.
lines: Create a queue and add the start node.
Mark the start node as visited.
While the queue is not empty, remove the front node.
Add each unvisited neighbor to the back of the queue and mark it visited.
questions.explanation: BFS keeps nodes in discovery order by adding new neighbors to the back and removing old nodes from the front.
